42	## 0.18.0
43	
44	- `callisto release plan --artifact-repository` without `--orchestration-revision` no longer fails as a usage error: a source with `[release]` fails with E231, and one without it ignores the flag.
45	- A private root `package.json` that starts with a byte-order mark is no longer listed as an npm package, which failed `status` with E013.
46	- `callisto completions` no longer offers a `help` subcommand at any depth, which `callisto pre` and `callisto release` do not accept.
47	- `callisto release --dry-run` now previews a release that builds artifacts when there is no `origin`, instead of failing with E170. A real release still needs one.
48	- A local `callisto release` could miss a package that changed since its version commit (E320) when an earlier package in the release spans more than one directory and had already changed. It now compares every directory of every package.
49	- With `--format json`, a failing `release plan`, `release execute`, `release artifact-manifest` or `release-pr` subcommand now reports its own `command` in the error, and every JSON error carries `dryRun`, like the success reports. The library crates change their public API with it (`format_error_json` takes the command and dry-run flag, and `GraphError::PreJsonRead` carries the path), so this release is a minor bump.
50	- The docs and specs now say what a bump does to a Cargo member that inherits its version (`version.workspace = true`): it gets a literal version of its own, and `[workspace.package]` is left as it is. E248, which no command emitted, is retired.
51	- `callisto init` now prints its warnings in text mode, such as the Changesets config keys it dropped, not only in the JSON report.
52	- The `setup-callisto` action now requires the release attestation to come from `refs/heads/main`, so an asset attested from another branch or a manually dispatched run no longer verifies.
53	- The generated matrix release workflow now checks out the release commit in its `plan`, `build-python` and `execute` jobs. A branch checkout left HEAD attached, so each of those commands stopped with E170 and the release could not run. An existing workflow needs `ref: ${{ github.sha }}` on those three checkouts.
54	- The napi group drift warnings now tell you to edit the group's members in `callisto.toml`. They used to say to run `callisto init`, which fails when `callisto.toml` already exists.
55	- Confirming an npm publish no longer times out with E157 for a restricted scoped package when the release action is given `NPM_TOKEN`.
56	- A release that publishes several npm packages no longer fails with E157 on a slow registry just because earlier publishes took long. Each publish now gets its full confirmation window from when it was issued, where before all of them shared one window that started at the first.
57	- `callisto release plan --from-release-commit` now checks the repository first, so a shallow clone fails with E266 and a SHA-256 repository with E265, not a lower-level read error.
58	- E115 now names the pre-release state file it could not read, including when `[changesets] dir` moves it.
59	- A successful `cargo publish` or `npm publish` is no longer reported as already published, and a failed `npm publish` counts as already published only when npm reports a version conflict, such as `E409` or `EPUBLISHCONFLICT`.
60	- `callisto release` no longer prints the version-control tool's error when it cannot read `origin` while checking for unpushed tags.
61	- A `url` on a `cargo` registry in `callisto.toml` is now rejected with E254. Callisto never routed cargo to it, so a release went to the registry in `.cargo/config.toml` or crates.io while the configuration said otherwise. Publishing an npm package with yarn when `callisto.toml` sets an npm registry `url` now stops with E168 before yarn runs, because `yarn npm publish` has no `--registry` and would have published to yarn's own registry; set `npmPublishRegistry` in `.yarnrc.yml` instead.
62	- Removes code nothing used, including five error codes no command emits any more (E008, E050, E253, E257, E258). The library crates lose the public items that went with it, which makes this a minor release.
63	- The release tag push names the full `refs/tags/` ref, so a branch with the same name as the tag can no longer make the push ambiguous.
64	- `callisto version` no longer drops the BOM or converts CRLF to LF in a Cargo workspace root manifest when it rewrites a workspace dependency. A changelog that only quotes a version heading (indented, or in a code block) no longer makes the release skip that version's entry. A package whose display name gains an ecosystem prefix keeps one title in its changelog. An npm `overrides` or `resolutions` value that is `$name` or has a protocol (`npm:`, `file:`, `catalog:`) is left as written.
65	
66	## 0.17.0
67	
68	- `release execute` given a manifest that seals Python files but no `--artifact-dir` now asks for the directory (E233) instead of telling you to drop both flags (E232).
69	- `release-pr commit-plan` now fails if a Git filter such as CRLF conversion changes a staged file's bytes, and rejects a staged symlink or submodule.
70	- A duration such as `confirm-timeout = "5é"` now fails with a clear error instead of crashing.
71	- `callisto version --emit-decision` no longer fails when a dependent is bumped because of a package published to both crates.io and npm.
72	- A Git failure while inferring versions from commits now stops `version` and names the failing command, instead of being skipped.
73	- A fixed-group package with no changelog section now gets generated release notes instead of borrowing the other members' entries.
74	- When other group members add entries to a release's notes, the package's own headings and paragraphs are kept, and a short entry is no longer dropped because it appears inside a longer one.
75	- With `--format json`, `error.path` now holds the file for init, apply, artifact, release-input and config errors that name one.
76	- A `[[package]]` or `[[package-set]]` `match` with a prefix other than `cargo/`, `npm/` or `pypi/` is now an error (E317).
77	- `pre exit` and `pre enter` now report E114, not E212, for a baseline that is not a valid version.
78	- Confirming a PyPI upload now stops at the registry's confirmation window, even when the index keeps asking to retry later.
79	- The release action's `pending_pr_label` input is removed; merged releases are found with `callisto release pending`, so nothing sets or reads that label. Delete the input from your workflow if you pass it.
80	- The setup action now fails, instead of installing the latest release, when it cannot list release tags to resolve its pinned version.
81	- `callisto status --check --strict` now fails on the same warnings as `callisto version --strict`, such as a napi target missing from its fixed group. Without `--strict` they stay warnings.
82	- A pnpm `workspace:*` dependency that matches no workspace package now warns instead of staying silent.
83	
84	## 0.16.0
85	
86	- Pinning a version over `version.workspace = true` keeps the comment above that line and the one after it.
87	- `version` now changes only the updated values in `package.json`, keeping inline arrays and objects in place for smaller release PR diffs.
88	- New `callisto release pending` lists merged release commits whose release never finished (a missing tag or an unpublished GitHub release), oldest first, so a release that stopped partway can be found and recovered. It reads the committed decision of each release commit and publishes nothing.
89	- Callisto now blocks a first release when the registry links the package name to another repository.
90	
91	  - The error names that repository.
92	  - If the package moved and is yours, tag its version commit before retrying.
93	- Publishing with Yarn now honors `publishConfig.registry` without failing on an unsupported `--registry` flag.
94	- Release planning is about twice as fast in large workspaces, including with `--dry-run`.
95	- Empty snapshot tags, or tags containing spaces or `/`, now fail with a clear fix instead of producing a malformed version or an internal error.
96	- Poetry dependency updates now preserve nearby comments.
97	- `init` now explains that defaults apply when there is no configuration to write.
98	- npm ranges with spaced comparators are now recognized. If a new dependency version falls outside the range, `version` stops and asks you to update it instead of silently leaving the dependent unchanged.
99	- A crate's first release now checks for a description and a license or license file before publishing, avoiding a partial release.
100	- Generated changelogs and release PR details now keep blank lines clean around nested bullets.
101	- `release` now warns when a package's latest tag exists locally but not on `origin`, including in `--dry-run`. This exposes an unfinished tag push instead of reporting `Nothing to release.`
102	- Cargo dependency updates now keep comments immediately above a version, including shared entries in `[workspace.dependencies]`.
103	- `release --dry-run` now returns its plan in a few seconds when an optional registry name check cannot respond.
104	- `init` now supports repositories with all packages in subdirectories and no top-level manifest.
105	- A release note that contains a heading line, or a code block opened on a bullet, is no longer cut short or run on into the older versions when it is shown or published.
106	- Release notes no longer stop at headings inside code blocks or indented list items. Changelogs with a byte order mark no longer gain a duplicate title.
107	- Callisto's GitHub release workflow can finish an interrupted release after `main` advances.
108	
109	  - It resumes from the merged release PR's commit.
110	  - It finishes older pending releases before preparing the next release PR.
111	- Python `~=` dependency updates keep the original precision: `~=1.2` becomes `~=2.0`, leaving later 2.x releases eligible.
112	- Named Cargo registry tokens now reach Cargo only. Git, the GitHub CLI and other publishing tools no longer inherit them.
113	
114	## 0.15.0
115	
116	- `callisto init --yes` now works with no other flags: packages version independently unless `--versioning fixed` is given, and a GitHub repository gets the release workflow unless `--no-workflow` is given. A single package is no longer asked how to version. If the unrequested workflow cannot be built, such as offline, `init` skips it with a warning instead of failing. After writing the workflow, `init` lists the repository secrets to add and the first commands to run, and the publishing guide has new sections on first publishes and on pulling a release.
117	- The GitHub release of a package in a fixed group now lists the changes recorded against the group's other members, each marked with its package, instead of only its own changelog section.
118	- A generated build matrix builds `x86_64-apple-darwin` on `macos-latest`, since GitHub has retired the `macos-13` runner it used. The proto plugin now installs the Intel macOS and arm64 Linux release binaries.
119	- A changeset with an entry that names no package in the workspace, such as a typo or a removed package, now applies none of its entries and says so. Before, its other entries were applied and the file stayed on disk, so every `version` run bumped those packages again. A Cargo crate with no version, such as an xtask, no longer stops every run with E013: it is skipped with a note.
120	- A release commit is now checked for what else it changes. Verification (E165) refuses a version commit that touches any path other than manifests, lockfiles, changelogs, changesets, `pre.json` and the decision file, so a release pull request can no longer carry a change to source, a build script, `.npmrc` or `.cargo/config.toml` under the cover of a bot-authored diff. Move such edits to a separate commit.
121	- The leftover `[init]` and `[release.profiles]` tables in `callisto.toml` are removed, and a config that still has one now fails to load, naming the key; move a profile's `forge-repository` to `[release]`. The no-op `setup_git_user` action input is removed, and the setup action no longer falls back to building unreleased `main` when a release cannot be installed. The job's OIDC request variables now reach only the package-manager tools, not cargo, git or gh.
122	
123	## 0.14.2
124	
125	- A release no longer waits past its confirmation window when a registry keeps asking to retry later. The run now gives up when the window ends, as the error already said.
126	- The help for `add --package` and `matrix --package` now shows the `ecosystem/name` form they require, and the contributor and publishing guides match.
127	
128	## 0.14.1
129	
130	- Release tags now record the package that made them and the git tree of each of its directories in the tag message, as Callisto-Package and Callisto-Tree lines. Nothing reads them yet, and tags without them keep working.
131	- Waiting for npm packages to appear is now one window of confirm-timeout for the whole release: a package that shows up along the way no longer restarts it, and the time spent checking the registry counts, so a slow registry cannot stretch the wait to several windows.
132	- `status`, `version` and `release` skip two history reads for tags made by a recent release. They still read them for every other tag, so older and hand-made tags behave as before.
133	
134	## 0.14.0
135	
136	- After publishing, Callisto looks for a new npm version right away and then at 15 seconds, 45 seconds, 2 minutes and 3 minutes, instead of every 30 seconds, so a release makes about five looks per window rather than seventeen. The window and `confirm-timeout` are unchanged.
137	- A release no longer stops with E319 when a dependent's range already covers the new version but cannot be raised, such as `*` or a bare Python requirement. A range that a rewrite would leave excluding the new version, such as `<2.0.0` for 2.0.0, now fails with E319 instead of being published.
138	- A `[[package]]` or `[[package-set]]` rule is now matched against a package's name in the rule's own ecosystem. For a dual Cargo and npm package whose npm name differs, such as the napi package `@orin-dx/michi` in a directory called `michi-node`, `npm/michi-node` used to apply to it silently while a `[[fixed-group]]` rejected the same spelling. It now matches nothing, the matched-no-packages warning suggests `npm/@orin-dx/michi`, and a group member's E108 does too.
139	- A `[registries.<name>]` entry for a custom registry must now set `kind` to `cargo`, `npm` or `pypi`; without it Callisto fails with E321 instead of silently reading the registry as npm. The built-in `cratesIo`, `npm` and `pypi` entries may leave it out and keep their own kind, so `[registries.cratesIo]` with only a `confirm-timeout` no longer turns the crates.io registry into an npm one.
140	- A release of several npm packages now waits for the registry once instead of once per package. Callisto publishes the npm packages back to back, a package after the dependency it follows without waiting for the registry to show that dependency, then looks at all of them together until each version is visible. Tags, GitHub releases and uploads still wait until every npm version they follow is shown, so nothing is announced early. A release of eight npm packages that took eight waits of up to six minutes now takes one. Cargo and PyPI publishes are still confirmed one at a time.
141	- status, version and release --dry-run read tags and manifests in a handful of git calls instead of several per package, so they take well under a second on workspaces with hundreds of packages.
142	- Workspaces with thousands of packages load and plan about a quarter faster: manifests are read and parsed on several threads, and package name lookups no longer slow down as the package count grows.
143	- A local release no longer tags a published version onto code that was never published when the package inherits its version from the workspace, has more than 100 edits to its manifest, or was merged after unrelated commits; a registry that cannot be read now stops the release. Signed commits no longer break change detection when log.showSignature is set.
144	- status decides whether a package changed since its last tag by comparing its directories with the tagged ones, so it takes a fraction of a second however many commits the repository has, and a change that was later reverted no longer counts as a change.
145	
146	## 0.13.0
147	
148	- The release pull request no longer says "All changes are backward compatible" when a package is below 1.0.0 and gets a minor bump. It says that minor bumps below 1.0.0 can include breaking changes and to read the changes first.
149	- A registry in callisto.toml can set `publish-timeout` (for example `publish-timeout = "5m"`) to change how long one publish command may run before Callisto stops it with E025. The default stays 15 minutes.
150	- When a run adopts a Cargo or npm version that is already published, Callisto now warns if the registry records a different repository for it than this repository's origin, since the name may belong to someone else's package. It still adopts the version. A registry that records no repository, and PyPI, are not checked.
151	- Release binaries are now published for Intel macOS (`x86_64-apple-darwin`) and arm64 Linux (`aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`) as well as the existing three, and the `setup-callisto` action downloads them on those machines instead of building from crates.io. An older release without the new asset still installs from crates.io.
152	
153	## 0.12.0
154	
155	- A `pypi` registry in `callisto.toml` can set `publish-url` when its upload endpoint differs from its simple index: Callisto reads releases from `url` and uploads to `publish-url`. Without it, `url` serves both, as before.
156	- A failed npm, Cargo or PyPI publish now shows what the publish tool printed to standard output, not only standard error. pnpm prints its errors there, so a failed pnpm publish used to end with `npm publish failed (exit 1):` and nothing after it. The output also appears live in the release log while the publish runs, instead of only after it ends.
157	- A release whose changelog exists but cannot be read now fails planning with E125 naming the file, instead of publishing generated notes in place of the changelog the release PR reviewed. A missing changelog, a missing version section and an empty section still fall back to generated notes, with the notice.
158	- A package that takes a name from a renamed or removed package, including one in another ecosystem, no longer takes over that package's pre-release baseline or release tags, so it is no longer skipped as already released. `status` says which tag was rejected and points to `previous-tag-templates`.
159	- A `[[fixed-group]]` or `[[linked-group]]` that lists one package under two of its names, such as a Cargo crate and its npm name in a dual package, is now rejected with E250 instead of being accepted silently.
160	- When a release stops because a registry or forge could not be observed (E176) or a publish is not yet visible (E157), the error names the operation in words, such as "tag of cargo/demo 0.10.0" or "registry publish to internal of npm/demo 1.0.0", and ends with the most recent failed command and the last 20 lines or 2 KiB of its stderr, with credentials redacted.
161	- A release no longer stops with E157 when npm shows a published version late. After each publish Callisto now waits for the version to appear, up to 6 minutes for npm and PyPI and 2 for Cargo, instead of about 30 seconds, and the wait applies to a rerun that finds the version already published. A registry that is slower can set `confirm-timeout` on its `[registries]` entry in callisto.toml, for example `confirm-timeout = "10m"`.
162	- `callisto version` now warns about a changeset entry that names a package that is not in the workspace, as `status` already did. The changeset stays on disk, and its other entries are applied again by the next `version` run, so fix or remove the entry.
163	- Inference from commits now stops with E315 in a shallow clone instead of planning a smaller bump from the history it can see. A workspace table written inline or with dotted keys is recognised as a Cargo workspace root, and a pnpm workspace is published with pnpm even where its lockfile is not committed. An unreadable `src/bin` no longer hides a binary from `callisto init`, and the napi target check reads the main package's own `package.json` wherever it is.
164	- `callisto --help` describes Callisto as a release manager for Cargo, npm and Python workspaces instead of Rust workspaces only.
165	- In pre-release mode, `version` no longer bumps a package again when its only changesets are already recorded in `pre.json`: a rerun with nothing new changes nothing, and `status` stops reporting it as pending. A new changeset produces the next prerelease. `release-pr decide` now refuses pre-release mode with E318 and a local-release fix, instead of opening a pull request that cannot release.
166	- npm prereleases now publish under the tag their version names: `1.0.0-beta.2` goes to `beta`, `2.0.0-rc.1` to `rc`, and `next` remains the fallback, instead of every prerelease landing on `next`. `release` now refuses a version that `callisto snapshot` wrote (E169), so a snapshot is never tagged or published.
167	- Workspaces below the repository root, such as `native/` or `rust/`, are now supported for Cargo, npm, pnpm and uv. A nested workspace decides which packages beneath it are packages by its own `members` and `exclude`, `workspaces`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or `[tool.uv.workspace]`, and a private versionless `package.json` that holds one is not a package. Cargo members inherit `version.workspace = true` and `{ workspace = true }` dependencies from it instead of failing with E313. `callisto version` refreshes and stages the lockfile nearest to each package, and a release commit is verified against it. A nested npm workspace without a lockfile publishes from its own directory, a lockfile beside a package no longer takes it out of its workspace, and `npm view` and a publish by directory run in that directory, so the version looked for and the version published come from the same `.npmrc`. A package that moves to a different `package.workspace` between two commits is verified against each commit's own workspace, an interrupted-run check finds a staged bump in the workspace the package named at `HEAD`, and a directory that cannot be opened for syncing after a write is reported instead of skipped.
168	- An error from a failing `git` or other helper command run while versioning no longer prints a credential that the command echoed, such as a token in an authenticated remote URL. Registry tool output shown in errors and the CI log also hides more credential shapes: `npm_`, `ghp_` and `github_pat_` tokens, PyPI API tokens, `Bearer` values and `.npmrc` auth lines, and the value of any environment variable named like `*_TOKEN`, `*_SECRET` or `*_PASSWORD`, even when it is not one of the variables Callisto reads itself.
169	- A directory that holds both a Cargo or npm manifest and a Python manifest now fails with a message that names the grammars in a fixed order and says to put the Python package in its own directory.
170	- A library that ignores its `Cargo.lock` can release again: `callisto version` refreshes the lockfile but no longer fails trying to stage it. A changelog or manifest that a `.gitignore` ignores now stops `version` before anything is written, naming the file, instead of failing after the edits. Two `callisto add` runs at the same moment can no longer replace each other's changeset.
171	- Package references now take the form `ecosystem/name`, such as `cargo/foo`, `npm/foo` or `pypi/foo`. The colon form, such as `cargo:foo`, is rejected with E316 naming the slash form, in `--package`, changeset entries, `pre.json` keys, group members, package rules, and the product and artifact packages. A bare name is rejected with E317 showing the form to write, in `callisto.toml` (a group, a `[[package]]` or `[[package-set]]` `match`, a product or artifact package) and in `callisto add --package` and `callisto matrix --package`, so a name can no longer become ambiguous when a package in another ecosystem later takes it; `release --package` already required it. A package-set glob names one ecosystem, so a rule for several ecosystems is one rule each. Changeset entries and `pre.json` keys keep native names.
172	- `callisto release` now stops with E320 instead of tagging a version that is already on the registry onto a later commit. After a run that stopped between publishing and tagging, a rerun on a newer commit that changed the package names the commit that set the version; checking that commit out and running `callisto release` again adopts the published version and tags it there. The check follows the commit that set the package's own literal version, so a version inherited from the workspace is not covered.
173	- The `status`, `version`, `snapshot` and `matrix` JSON reports now name every package `ecosystem/name`, such as `cargo/foo`, for its primary ecosystem, whether or not another ecosystem shares the name. This covers bumps, cascade reasons, diagnostics and the `matrix` map keys. These four reports now carry `schemaVersion` 2; the other reports still carry 1. Text output follows. Changeset entries, `pre.json` keys and default tags are unchanged.
174	- `callisto schema` now prints JSON Schema draft 2020-12: shared definitions live under `$defs` instead of `definitions`, and a fixed string variant is written as `const` instead of a one-element `enum`. The shapes the schemas accept are unchanged.
175	- A Poetry caret or tilde dependency on a Python package released together with it, such as `core-py = "^0.1.0"`, is now rewritten to cover the new version instead of being left behind with a warning. 376	  - Release intents are schema v5 and run envelopes v3; re-plan intents made by older versions.
377	- **`release plan` checks what `publish` checks**
378	  
379	  Release planning now rejects an untrusted or non-https npm `publishConfig.registry`, requires an unreleased npm platform dependency to be selected with its owner, orders dev-only dependency cycles instead of failing, publishes scoped npm packages as public by default, and uses the changelog section as GitHub release notes (falling back to generated notes with a stderr notice).
380	  
381	  Breaking:
382	  - `--package` for a package with no pending release fails with "nothing pending to release"; one with no publish target fails with "no publish target"; a name not in the workspace is an unknown package.
383	  - `release plan` fails with E199 for a `publish-to` target it cannot dispatch (NuGet) instead of skipping it.
384	  - `callisto_graph::commands::registry_argv::npm_publish_directory_argv` takes the package name.
385	- The release PR action commits exactly the staged content and works when run from a subdirectory; a mismatch fails with E059.
386	- A release rerun adopts an existing annotated tag on the right commit even when its message differs, instead of failing depending on whether the tag had been fetched.
387	- **Rerunning a failed release completes it**
388	  
389	  `release execute` now adopts every effect that already landed, including a published registry version (one warning line each), and builds the receipt from in-memory execution state, so "Re-run failed jobs" finishes a partial release instead of failing with E174. Execution state is no longer persisted, and E173 and E174 are gone.
390	  
391	  Breaking:
392	  - `release execute --recovery` and `--state` are removed.
393	  - `release reconcile` and `callisto schema --type release-state` are removed.
394	  - The receipt's run envelope drops `kind` and is envelope schema v2.
395	- Output that explains why a package is released reports `release-trigger = changeset` as the default, not `auto`.
396	- **Release trust allows gitignored build output**
397	  
398	  A release no longer aborts because a gitignored path exists (built `.node` files, `dist/`, `node_modules/`). Modified tracked files and untracked files still block it, and the error names the path.
399	- Every CLI error now carries a numeric E#### code instead of a callisto::name string
400	- A malformed release intent file (duplicate operation, cycle, mismatched artifact roster, digest mismatch, or unsupported trust profile) reports its own specific error code from release verify and release execute, instead of one generic code for every case.
401	- **One build: every ecosystem and commit inference always compiled in**
402	  
403	  Commit inference now ships in the release binary. It runs only for packages with `release-trigger = "auto"`; the default `changeset` trigger is unchanged.
404	  
405	  Breaking:
406	  - Removed Cargo features `cargo`, `npm`, `inference` (`callisto-cli`, `callisto-graph`) and `cargo`, `npm`, `pypi`, `go`, `maven`, `nuget`, `deno` (`callisto-manifests`).
407	- `callisto init` now generates a release workflow for workspaces that ship `[[release.artifact]]` binaries or napi platform packages, instead of skipping them. The file is `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` with four jobs: `version-pr`, `plan` (`callisto release plan`), `build` (a matrix of the napi targets from `callisto matrix` plus one entry per artifact slot in the release intent) and `execute` (`napi artifacts`, then `callisto release artifact-manifest`, then `callisto release execute`). In npm workspaces, `execute` sets `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` so npm publishes carry provenance. Planning runs only when the pushed commit writes `.callisto/release-decision.json`, so ordinary pushes leave `plan`, `build` and `execute` skipped.
408	  
409	  Workspaces with maturin platform builds, or with platform packages and no `napi.targets`, still get no generated workflow. Passing `--workflow` for one of them fails with E202 and names the reason. Otherwise `init` skips the question and prints a note, which also appears in `InitReport.diagnostics` as `workflow-generation-unsupported`.
410	  
411	  `callisto matrix --format json` now lists each cargo `[[release.artifact]]` binary as a `cargo` entry in `platformTargets`, with the slot's asset name as its `artifactName`. A package that declares both platform targets and release artifacts fails with E203. A cargo `[[release.artifact]]` naming no workspace package is reported as an `unknown-package` warning instead of being dropped silently.

# callisto-cli

## 0.19.0

_2026-11-09 · [compare](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/compare/callisto@0.18.0...callisto@0.19.0)_

### Minor Changes

- Changelogs group each release's changes by bump, so they are easier to scan.

  - Major, Minor and Patch Changes headings
  - The release date, plus a link to compare with the previous version when the GitHub repository is known
  - A package that only released with its group gets one line saying so

  **Upgrading**
  - To keep the old single list, set `layout = "flat"` under `[changelog]` in `callisto.toml`.
- The release PR tells you what to expect before you merge.

  **What you see**
  - Changes grouped under Major, Minor and Patch, each titled by its first line instead of its file name, with long notes folded away
  - A "Read before merging" block listing `Breaking:` and `Action:` notes, a `Breaking:` note whose bump is too low, and packages that changed but are not in this release
  - Where merging will publish each package, with a warning if the release would be refused
  - Labels such as `callisto: ready`, `blocked` and `bump: minor`, so you can triage without opening the PR
    - Missing labels are created, and labels that stop applying are removed

  **Scripting**
  - `callisto version --emit-preview <path>` writes the release as JSON
  - `compose-pr-body --preview <path>` builds the PR body from that file
    - Relative paths resolve against `--cwd`
  - `compose-pr-body --publish-plan` adds the publish section; the release PR action already passes it

  **Upgrading**
  - Nothing to change. Start a changeset paragraph with `Breaking:` or `Action:` to have it listed.

### Patch Changes

- Relative file flags of `release` and `release-pr` now follow `--cwd`.

  - Before, they resolved against the directory you ran from.
  - If a script passes relative paths together with `--cwd`, make them relative to that directory or absolute.

## 0.18.0

- `callisto release plan --artifact-repository` without `--orchestration-revision` no longer fails as a usage error: a source with `[release]` fails with E231, and one without it ignores the flag.
- A private root `package.json` that starts with a byte-order mark is no longer listed as an npm package, which failed `status` with E013.
- `callisto completions` no longer offers a `help` subcommand at any depth, which `callisto pre` and `callisto release` do not accept.
- `callisto release --dry-run` now previews a release that builds artifacts when there is no `origin`, instead of failing with E170. A real release still needs one.
- A local `callisto release` could miss a package that changed since its version commit (E320) when an earlier package in the release spans more than one directory and had already changed. It now compares every directory of every package.
- With `--format json`, a failing `release plan`, `release execute`, `release artifact-manifest` or `release-pr` subcommand now reports its own `command` in the error, and every JSON error carries `dryRun`, like the success reports. The library crates change their public API with it (`format_error_json` takes the command and dry-run flag, and `GraphError::PreJsonRead` carries the path), so this release is a minor bump.
- The docs and specs now say what a bump does to a Cargo member that inherits its version (`version.workspace = true`): it gets a literal version of its own, and `[workspace.package]` is left as it is. E248, which no command emitted, is retired.
- `callisto init` now prints its warnings in text mode, such as the Changesets config keys it dropped, not only in the JSON report.
- The `setup-callisto` action now requires the release attestation to come from `refs/heads/main`, so an asset attested from another branch or a manually dispatched run no longer verifies.
- The generated matrix release workflow now checks out the release commit in its `plan`, `build-python` and `execute` jobs. A branch checkout left HEAD attached, so each of those commands stopped with E170 and the release could not run. An existing workflow needs `ref: ${{ github.sha }}` on those three checkouts.
- The napi group drift warnings now tell you to edit the group's members in `callisto.toml`. They used to say to run `callisto init`, which fails when `callisto.toml` already exists.
- Confirming an npm publish no longer times out with E157 for a restricted scoped package when the release action is given `NPM_TOKEN`.
- A release that publishes several npm packages no longer fails with E157 on a slow registry just because earlier publishes took long. Each publish now gets its full confirmation window from when it was issued, where before all of them shared one window that started at the first.
- `callisto release plan --from-release-commit` now checks the repository first, so a shallow clone fails with E266 and a SHA-256 repository with E265, not a lower-level read error.
- E115 now names the pre-release state file it could not read, including when `[changesets] dir` moves it.
- A successful `cargo publish` or `npm publish` is no longer reported as already published, and a failed `npm publish` counts as already published only when npm reports a version conflict, such as `E409` or `EPUBLISHCONFLICT`.
- `callisto release` no longer prints the version-control tool's error when it cannot read `origin` while checking for unpushed tags.
- A `url` on a `cargo` registry in `callisto.toml` is now rejected with E254. Callisto never routed cargo to it, so a release went to the registry in `.cargo/config.toml` or crates.io while the configuration said otherwise. Publishing an npm package with yarn when `callisto.toml` sets an npm registry `url` now stops with E168 before yarn runs, because `yarn npm publish` has no `--registry` and would have published to yarn's own registry; set `npmPublishRegistry` in `.yarnrc.yml` instead.
- Removes code nothing used, including five error codes no command emits any more (E008, E050, E253, E257, E258). The library crates lose the public items that went with it, which makes this a minor release.
- The release tag push names the full `refs/tags/` ref, so a branch with the same name as the tag can no longer make the push ambiguous.
- `callisto version` no longer drops the BOM or converts CRLF to LF in a Cargo workspace root manifest when it rewrites a workspace dependency. A changelog that only quotes a version heading (indented, or in a code block) no longer makes the release skip that version's entry. A package whose display name gains an ecosystem prefix keeps one title in its changelog. An npm `overrides` or `resolutions` value that is `$name` or has a protocol (`npm:`, `file:`, `catalog:`) is left as written.

## 0.17.0

- `release execute` given a manifest that seals Python files but no `--artifact-dir` now asks for the directory (E233) instead of telling you to drop both flags (E232).
- `release-pr commit-plan` now fails if a Git filter such as CRLF conversion changes a staged file's bytes, and rejects a staged symlink or submodule.
- A duration such as `confirm-timeout = "5é"` now fails with a clear error instead of crashing.
- `callisto version --emit-decision` no longer fails when a dependent is bumped because of a package published to both crates.io and npm.
- A Git failure while inferring versions from commits now stops `version` and names the failing command, instead of being skipped.
- A fixed-group package with no changelog section now gets generated release notes instead of borrowing the other members' entries.
- When other group members add entries to a release's notes, the package's own headings and paragraphs are kept, and a short entry is no longer dropped because it appears inside a longer one.
- With `--format json`, `error.path` now holds the file for init, apply, artifact, release-input and config errors that name one.
- A `[[package]]` or `[[package-set]]` `match` with a prefix other than `cargo/`, `npm/` or `pypi/` is now an error (E317).
- `pre exit` and `pre enter` now report E114, not E212, for a baseline that is not a valid version.
- Confirming a PyPI upload now stops at the registry's confirmation window, even when the index keeps asking to retry later.
- The release action's `pending_pr_label` input is removed; merged releases are found with `callisto release pending`, so nothing sets or reads that label. Delete the input from your workflow if you pass it.
- The setup action now fails, instead of installing the latest release, when it cannot list release tags to resolve its pinned version.
- `callisto status --check --strict` now fails on the same warnings as `callisto version --strict`, such as a napi target missing from its fixed group. Without `--strict` they stay warnings.
- A pnpm `workspace:*` dependency that matches no workspace package now warns instead of staying silent.

## 0.16.0

- Pinning a version over `version.workspace = true` keeps the comment above that line and the one after it.
- `version` now changes only the updated values in `package.json`, keeping inline arrays and objects in place for smaller release PR diffs.
- New `callisto release pending` lists merged release commits whose release never finished (a missing tag or an unpublished GitHub release), oldest first, so a release that stopped partway can be found and recovered. It reads the committed decision of each release commit and publishes nothing.
- Callisto now blocks a first release when the registry links the package name to another repository.

  - The error names that repository.
  - If the package moved and is yours, tag its version commit before retrying.
- Publishing with Yarn now honors `publishConfig.registry` without failing on an unsupported `--registry` flag.
- Release planning is about twice as fast in large workspaces, including with `--dry-run`.
- Empty snapshot tags, or tags containing spaces or `/`, now fail with a clear fix instead of producing a malformed version or an internal error.
- Poetry dependency updates now preserve nearby comments.
- `init` now explains that defaults apply when there is no configuration to write.
- npm ranges with spaced comparators are now recognized. If a new dependency version falls outside the range, `version` stops and asks you to update it instead of silently leaving the dependent unchanged.
- A crate's first release now checks for a description and a license or license file before publishing, avoiding a partial release.
- Generated changelogs and release PR details now keep blank lines clean around nested bullets.
- `release` now warns when a package's latest tag exists locally but not on `origin`, including in `--dry-run`. This exposes an unfinished tag push instead of reporting `Nothing to release.`
- Cargo dependency updates now keep comments immediately above a version, including shared entries in `[workspace.dependencies]`.
- `release --dry-run` now returns its plan in a few seconds when an optional registry name check cannot respond.
- `init` now supports repositories with all packages in subdirectories and no top-level manifest.
- A release note that contains a heading line, or a code block opened on a bullet, is no longer cut short or run on into the older versions when it is shown or published.
- Release notes no longer stop at headings inside code blocks or indented list items. Changelogs with a byte order mark no longer gain a duplicate title.
- Callisto's GitHub release workflow can finish an interrupted release after `main` advances.

  - It resumes from the merged release PR's commit.
  - It finishes older pending releases before preparing the next release PR.
- Python `~=` dependency updates keep the original precision: `~=1.2` becomes `~=2.0`, leaving later 2.x releases eligible.
- Named Cargo registry tokens now reach Cargo only. Git, the GitHub CLI and other publishing tools no longer inherit them.

## 0.15.0

- `callisto init --yes` now works with no other flags: packages version independently unless `--versioning fixed` is given, and a GitHub repository gets the release workflow unless `--no-workflow` is given. A single package is no longer asked how to version. If the unrequested workflow cannot be built, such as offline, `init` skips it with a warning instead of failing. After writing the workflow, `init` lists the repository secrets to add and the first commands to run, and the publishing guide has new sections on first publishes and on pulling a release.
- The GitHub release of a package in a fixed group now lists the changes recorded against the group's other members, each marked with its package, instead of only its own changelog section.
- A generated build matrix builds `x86_64-apple-darwin` on `macos-latest`, since GitHub has retired the `macos-13` runner it used. The proto plugin now installs the Intel macOS and arm64 Linux release binaries.
- A changeset with an entry that names no package in the workspace, such as a typo or a removed package, now applies none of its entries and says so. Before, its other entries were applied and the file stayed on disk, so every `version` run bumped those packages again. A Cargo crate with no version, such as an xtask, no longer stops every run with E013: it is skipped with a note.
- A release commit is now checked for what else it changes. Verification (E165) refuses a version commit that touches any path other than manifests, lockfiles, changelogs, changesets, `pre.json` and the decision file, so a release pull request can no longer carry a change to source, a build script, `.npmrc` or `.cargo/config.toml` under the cover of a bot-authored diff. Move such edits to a separate commit.
- The leftover `[init]` and `[release.profiles]` tables in `callisto.toml` are removed, and a config that still has one now fails to load, naming the key; move a profile's `forge-repository` to `[release]`. The no-op `setup_git_user` action input is removed, and the setup action no longer falls back to building unreleased `main` when a release cannot be installed. The job's OIDC request variables now reach only the package-manager tools, not cargo, git or gh.

## 0.14.2

- A release no longer waits past its confirmation window when a registry keeps asking to retry later. The run now gives up when the window ends, as the error already said.
- The help for `add --package` and `matrix --package` now shows the `ecosystem/name` form they require, and the contributor and publishing guides match.

## 0.14.1

- Release tags now record the package that made them and the git tree of each of its directories in the tag message, as Callisto-Package and Callisto-Tree lines. Nothing reads them yet, and tags without them keep working.
- Waiting for npm packages to appear is now one window of confirm-timeout for the whole release: a package that shows up along the way no longer restarts it, and the time spent checking the registry counts, so a slow registry cannot stretch the wait to several windows.
- `status`, `version` and `release` skip two history reads for tags made by a recent release. They still read them for every other tag, so older and hand-made tags behave as before.

## 0.14.0

- After publishing, Callisto looks for a new npm version right away and then at 15 seconds, 45 seconds, 2 minutes and 3 minutes, instead of every 30 seconds, so a release makes about five looks per window rather than seventeen. The window and `confirm-timeout` are unchanged.
- A release no longer stops with E319 when a dependent's range already covers the new version but cannot be raised, such as `*` or a bare Python requirement. A range that a rewrite would leave excluding the new version, such as `<2.0.0` for 2.0.0, now fails with E319 instead of being published.
- A `[[package]]` or `[[package-set]]` rule is now matched against a package's name in the rule's own ecosystem. For a dual Cargo and npm package whose npm name differs, such as the napi package `@orin-dx/michi` in a directory called `michi-node`, `npm/michi-node` used to apply to it silently while a `[[fixed-group]]` rejected the same spelling. It now matches nothing, the matched-no-packages warning suggests `npm/@orin-dx/michi`, and a group member's E108 does too.
- A `[registries.<name>]` entry for a custom registry must now set `kind` to `cargo`, `npm` or `pypi`; without it Callisto fails with E321 instead of silently reading the registry as npm. The built-in `cratesIo`, `npm` and `pypi` entries may leave it out and keep their own kind, so `[registries.cratesIo]` with only a `confirm-timeout` no longer turns the crates.io registry into an npm one.
- A release of several npm packages now waits for the registry once instead of once per package. Callisto publishes the npm packages back to back, a package after the dependency it follows without waiting for the registry to show that dependency, then looks at all of them together until each version is visible. Tags, GitHub releases and uploads still wait until every npm version they follow is shown, so nothing is announced early. A release of eight npm packages that took eight waits of up to six minutes now takes one. Cargo and PyPI publishes are still confirmed one at a time.
- status, version and release --dry-run read tags and manifests in a handful of git calls instead of several per package, so they take well under a second on workspaces with hundreds of packages.
- Workspaces with thousands of packages load and plan about a quarter faster: manifests are read and parsed on several threads, and package name lookups no longer slow down as the package count grows.
- A local release no longer tags a published version onto code that was never published when the package inherits its version from the workspace, has more than 100 edits to its manifest, or was merged after unrelated commits; a registry that cannot be read now stops the release. Signed commits no longer break change detection when log.showSignature is set.
- status decides whether a package changed since its last tag by comparing its directories with the tagged ones, so it takes a fraction of a second however many commits the repository has, and a change that was later reverted no longer counts as a change.

## 0.13.0

- The release pull request no longer says "All changes are backward compatible" when a package is below 1.0.0 and gets a minor bump. It says that minor bumps below 1.0.0 can include breaking changes and to read the changes first.
- A registry in callisto.toml can set `publish-timeout` (for example `publish-timeout = "5m"`) to change how long one publish command may run before Callisto stops it with E025. The default stays 15 minutes.
- When a run adopts a Cargo or npm version that is already published, Callisto now warns if the registry records a different repository for it than this repository's origin, since the name may belong to someone else's package. It still adopts the version. A registry that records no repository, and PyPI, are not checked.
- Release binaries are now published for Intel macOS (`x86_64-apple-darwin`) and arm64 Linux (`aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`) as well as the existing three, and the `setup-callisto` action downloads them on those machines instead of building from crates.io. An older release without the new asset still installs from crates.io.

## 0.12.0

- A `pypi` registry in `callisto.toml` can set `publish-url` when its upload endpoint differs from its simple index: Callisto reads releases from `url` and uploads to `publish-url`. Without it, `url` serves both, as before.
- A failed npm, Cargo or PyPI publish now shows what the publish tool printed to standard output, not only standard error. pnpm prints its errors there, so a failed pnpm publish used to end with `npm publish failed (exit 1):` and nothing after it. The output also appears live in the release log while the publish runs, instead of only after it ends.
- A release whose changelog exists but cannot be read now fails planning with E125 naming the file, instead of publishing generated notes in place of the changelog the release PR reviewed. A missing changelog, a missing version section and an empty section still fall back to generated notes, with the notice.
- A package that takes a name from a renamed or removed package, including one in another ecosystem, no longer takes over that package's pre-release baseline or release tags, so it is no longer skipped as already released. `status` says which tag was rejected and points to `previous-tag-templates`.
- A `[[fixed-group]]` or `[[linked-group]]` that lists one package under two of its names, such as a Cargo crate and its npm name in a dual package, is now rejected with E250 instead of being accepted silently.
- When a release stops because a registry or forge could not be observed (E176) or a publish is not yet visible (E157), the error names the operation in words, such as "tag of cargo/demo 0.10.0" or "registry publish to internal of npm/demo 1.0.0", and ends with the most recent failed command and the last 20 lines or 2 KiB of its stderr, with credentials redacted.
- A release no longer stops with E157 when npm shows a published version late. After each publish Callisto now waits for the version to appear, up to 6 minutes for npm and PyPI and 2 for Cargo, instead of about 30 seconds, and the wait applies to a rerun that finds the version already published. A registry that is slower can set `confirm-timeout` on its `[registries]` entry in callisto.toml, for example `confirm-timeout = "10m"`.
- `callisto version` now warns about a changeset entry that names a package that is not in the workspace, as `status` already did. The changeset stays on disk, and its other entries are applied again by the next `version` run, so fix or remove the entry.
- Inference from commits now stops with E315 in a shallow clone instead of planning a smaller bump from the history it can see. A workspace table written inline or with dotted keys is recognised as a Cargo workspace root, and a pnpm workspace is published with pnpm even where its lockfile is not committed. An unreadable `src/bin` no longer hides a binary from `callisto init`, and the napi target check reads the main package's own `package.json` wherever it is.
- `callisto --help` describes Callisto as a release manager for Cargo, npm and Python workspaces instead of Rust workspaces only.
- In pre-release mode, `version` no longer bumps a package again when its only changesets are already recorded in `pre.json`: a rerun with nothing new changes nothing, and `status` stops reporting it as pending. A new changeset produces the next prerelease. `release-pr decide` now refuses pre-release mode with E318 and a local-release fix, instead of opening a pull request that cannot release.
- npm prereleases now publish under the tag their version names: `1.0.0-beta.2` goes to `beta`, `2.0.0-rc.1` to `rc`, and `next` remains the fallback, instead of every prerelease landing on `next`. `release` now refuses a version that `callisto snapshot` wrote (E169), so a snapshot is never tagged or published.
- Workspaces below the repository root, such as `native/` or `rust/`, are now supported for Cargo, npm, pnpm and uv. A nested workspace decides which packages beneath it are packages by its own `members` and `exclude`, `workspaces`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or `[tool.uv.workspace]`, and a private versionless `package.json` that holds one is not a package. Cargo members inherit `version.workspace = true` and `{ workspace = true }` dependencies from it instead of failing with E313. `callisto version` refreshes and stages the lockfile nearest to each package, and a release commit is verified against it. A nested npm workspace without a lockfile publishes from its own directory, a lockfile beside a package no longer takes it out of its workspace, and `npm view` and a publish by directory run in that directory, so the version looked for and the version published come from the same `.npmrc`. A package that moves to a different `package.workspace` between two commits is verified against each commit's own workspace, an interrupted-run check finds a staged bump in the workspace the package named at `HEAD`, and a directory that cannot be opened for syncing after a write is reported instead of skipped.
- An error from a failing `git` or other helper command run while versioning no longer prints a credential that the command echoed, such as a token in an authenticated remote URL. Registry tool output shown in errors and the CI log also hides more credential shapes: `npm_`, `ghp_` and `github_pat_` tokens, PyPI API tokens, `Bearer` values and `.npmrc` auth lines, and the value of any environment variable named like `*_TOKEN`, `*_SECRET` or `*_PASSWORD`, even when it is not one of the variables Callisto reads itself.
- A directory that holds both a Cargo or npm manifest and a Python manifest now fails with a message that names the grammars in a fixed order and says to put the Python package in its own directory.
- A library that ignores its `Cargo.lock` can release again: `callisto version` refreshes the lockfile but no longer fails trying to stage it. A changelog or manifest that a `.gitignore` ignores now stops `version` before anything is written, naming the file, instead of failing after the edits. Two `callisto add` runs at the same moment can no longer replace each other's changeset.
- Package references now take the form `ecosystem/name`, such as `cargo/foo`, `npm/foo` or `pypi/foo`. The colon form, such as `cargo:foo`, is rejected with E316 naming the slash form, in `--package`, changeset entries, `pre.json` keys, group members, package rules, and the product and artifact packages. A bare name is rejected with E317 showing the form to write, in `callisto.toml` (a group, a `[[package]]` or `[[package-set]]` `match`, a product or artifact package) and in `callisto add --package` and `callisto matrix --package`, so a name can no longer become ambiguous when a package in another ecosystem later takes it; `release --package` already required it. A package-set glob names one ecosystem, so a rule for several ecosystems is one rule each. Changeset entries and `pre.json` keys keep native names.
- `callisto release` now stops with E320 instead of tagging a version that is already on the registry onto a later commit. After a run that stopped between publishing and tagging, a rerun on a newer commit that changed the package names the commit that set the version; checking that commit out and running `callisto release` again adopts the published version and tags it there. The check follows the commit that set the package's own literal version, so a version inherited from the workspace is not covered.
- The `status`, `version`, `snapshot` and `matrix` JSON reports now name every package `ecosystem/name`, such as `cargo/foo`, for its primary ecosystem, whether or not another ecosystem shares the name. This covers bumps, cascade reasons, diagnostics and the `matrix` map keys. These four reports now carry `schemaVersion` 2; the other reports still carry 1. Text output follows. Changeset entries, `pre.json` keys and default tags are unchanged.
- `callisto schema` now prints JSON Schema draft 2020-12: shared definitions live under `$defs` instead of `definitions`, and a fixed string variant is written as `const` instead of a one-element `enum`. The shapes the schemas accept are unchanged.
- A Poetry caret or tilde dependency on a Python package released together with it, such as `core-py = "^0.1.0"`, is now rewritten to cover the new version instead of being left behind with a warning. A range that spans a single minor, such as `core-py>=0.1.0,<0.2`, stays one minor wide (`>=0.2.0, <0.3`) instead of widening to the next major.
- `status` now warns when a package has a pending release inferred from commits but no changeset names it. The release pull request reads changesets only, so it would never release that package. `status --check --strict` fails on it.
- The release workflow `callisto init` generates for a simple workspace now runs one release at a time, so two pushes to the default branch in a row no longer race to tag and publish the same versions.
- `version` and `snapshot` now stop with E319 before writing anything when a dependency range that consumers install would keep excluding the new version cannot be rewritten, such as a Cargo `>=1.2.0, <2.0.0` range after a major bump. It used to warn, release the dependent anyway and leave an unresolvable range. An npm range with a prerelease clause, such as `^2.0.0-next.0` left over from a prerelease cycle, is now rewritten like any other (`^3.0.0`). Dev dependencies still only warn.
- A package published to several registries now orders each distribution on its own. A dependent follows only the distribution it depends on: a Cargo dependent follows the crate and an npm dependent follows the npm package, so a failed publish in one ecosystem no longer holds back dependents in the other. A product's GitHub release is no longer made public before the registry publishes of a plugin package whose asset it carries have finished. `callisto release --package` on one distribution, such as `npm/dual`, releases every distribution of that package, so its shared tag and GitHub release no longer follow a single publish. An intent planned by an older version is rejected as stale and needs `release plan` again.
- The published crates now declare their minimum Rust version, keywords and categories, and no longer ship their test files, so crates.io shows the right metadata and installs download less.

## 0.11.0

- A Python release that stopped partway is completed on rerun. Only the files PyPI lacks are uploaded, and the release counts as published only when both the wheel and the sdist it builds are on the index, so no tag is created for a half-published release. Uploads name their files instead of a dist glob, so a stale dist directory is no longer published.
  
  Breaking: `callisto_graph`'s `registry_argv::pypi_publish_argv` is replaced by `pypi_build_argv` and `pypi_upload_argv`.
- A package that sits behind a symbolic link is now rejected with an error naming it, because Git cannot stage a change to a file beneath a link and the version bump could never be committed. A link that holds no package is ignored, and a link can be skipped by listing it in a `.gitignore` under the workspace root.
- A failed Git lookup is now an error instead of "nothing there". A broken or missing repository used to read as no tags, no such ref, no file at that revision or no matches, so `status` and `version` could plan from the wrong history without saying so. Only Git's own "not found" answer counts as absent now, a tag that is listed but does not resolve to a commit stops the run, and `status` warns once about each tag that matches a package's tag template but is not a version.
- Generated release workflows now install the Python build and upload tools they need. A workspace that publishes to PyPI no longer depends on `twine` being preinstalled on the runner.
- A package published to both Cargo and npm now gets its tag and GitHub release only after both publishes succeed, instead of after the first.
- `callisto add` no longer overwrites an existing changeset when it draws a name that is already taken, and a file Callisto rewrites keeps its permissions (it was left owner-only). A command whose output was cut short because a background process kept its pipes open is now an error instead of a success with empty output. Workspace globs written as `./packages/*` or `packages/*/` now match the same directories as `packages/*`.
- A package published to both Cargo and npm now gets one git tag and one GitHub release. A release that also uploads assets, which failed to plan with a repeated artifact slot, now plans and runs.
- A PyPI token or npm config token that a publish tool echoes in an error is now redacted from the output, like the other registry tokens.
- Callisto now stops, naming the file, when a workspace manifest is malformed instead of guessing which packages it contains. An unreadable or unparseable root `Cargo.toml`, `pyproject.toml`, `package.json` or `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and a `members`, `exclude`, `workspaces` or `packages` entry that is not a valid list of globs, fail the command; before, they silently admitted every directory, so vendored copies and excluded crates became releasable packages. Locating the workspace root also no longer skips a malformed manifest and settles on a different root.
- **A Cargo dependency declared in several tables is followed and rewritten in each**
  
  A dependency declared more than once, for example in `[dependencies]` and in a `[target.<cfg>.dependencies]` table with different constraints, now cascades to its dependent and is rewritten in every table when the package it names is released. Before, only the first declaration was updated and another one kept a stale constraint. A target declaration whose range still covers the new version now has its lower bound raised, as a plain declaration does. A Python requirement declared more than once, in the project dependencies, in several extras, in Poetry's table or under different markers, is followed and rewritten in each place by its own constraint, so a loose line such as `lib-py>=0.1` has its floor raised to `>=0.2.0` rather than being skipped.
  
  Breaking:
  - `callisto_model`: `DependencyEntry` and `DepEdge` gain a `locator: DepLocator` field naming the table a declaration lives in. `DepLocator` is a `#[non_exhaustive]` enum, `Unspecified` (the default, for npm), `Cargo` or `Python`: build it with `DepLocator::cargo` or `DepLocator::python`. The new `DepContainer` names the Python table. A writer given a locator for another ecosystem returns `DependencyNotFound`.
  - `callisto_manifests`: `Manifest::update_dependency_spec` takes the declaration's `&DepLocator` after the dependency kind.
  - `callisto_graph`: `RewriteKey` gains a `locator` field.
- Yarn classic's `"workspaces": { "packages": [...] }` form is now read for workspace membership, and a root Cargo workspace that cannot be loaded for version inheritance is reported instead of silently dropping the packages that inherit from it.
- Callisto no longer plans a release from a workspace it could only partly read. A package whose manifest cannot be opened (for example a member that inherits its version from a Rust workspace Callisto cannot find) used to keep no publish target and no dependency edges, so it never published and its dependents never cascaded, without a message. Every command now stops with a coded error naming each such manifest.
- A release workflow that builds Python distributions in a job without registry credentials now publishes exactly those files. The generated build-matrix workflow gains a `build-python` job, the manifest records each file's name, size and sha256, and a file PyPI already holds under a sealed name with different bytes stops the release before any upload. Python builds also set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` to the release commit time.
- callisto status now reads a changeset's package names the same way callisto version does. A package named by a non-primary manifest's own name resolves, a qualified name for an ecosystem the package lacks is reported as unknown, and a name that two packages claim is ambiguous, so status --check no longer passes a changeset that version will not consume.
- A release now stops with a clear error when git cannot read the local tag state, for example a corrupt or unreadable repository, or when npm cannot be reached or rejects the version lookup, instead of treating the version as unpublished and attempting to publish or tag. npm 8 and later still report a missing version as unpublished.
- A file Callisto cannot read or look up is now reported instead of treated as missing. An unreadable package manifest, `callisto.toml`, `pre.json` or changelog, a changeset it cannot inspect, and a failed directory sync after a write now stop the command with the file named, where before the package, config, changeset or durability guarantee was silently dropped.
- A release that stops because a provider could not be observed now says why: the HTTP status the registry or forge answered, a failed command, an answer it could not understand, or a timeout.
- `version` now checks every file it is about to write before it writes the first one. A manifest that is missing, unreadable, a directory, in an unwritable folder, or reached through a symbolic link Git cannot stage stops the command with every such file named and nothing changed, instead of failing partway through and leaving some manifests already bumped.
- A pre-release state that records two different starting versions for one package, for example an old bare key and its qualified key, now stops with an error naming both keys and versions instead of silently keeping one.
- A package keeps its release history when its directory moves, when it gains a higher-priority manifest beside a same-named package, or when a same-named sibling is removed. Before, the last release was reported as none, or an older release was chosen over a newer one, so already-released work could be released again.
  
  Breaking:
  - `callisto_graph`: `TagIndex::build` takes the workspace's `&IdentityIndex` after the graph.

## 0.10.3

- A release rerun adopts a local tag whose message has several paragraphs or a signature, instead of failing while reading it.
- A rerun after a failed tag push now completes the release. A tag that exists on the release commit no longer hides unfinished work: the push, GitHub release and any other missing steps are performed and the receipt is written.
- The generated build-matrix release workflow builds and places napi addons only for packages in the release. An unrelated or misconfigured napi addon no longer adds builds or fails the plan job of a release that does not include it.

## 0.10.2

- Releases that ship artifacts no longer fail with E140: the GitHub CLI that checks attestations and publishes the release keeps its own token instead of running unauthenticated.

## 0.10.1

- Generated npm and PyPI releases configure native registry authentication for publishing without exposing credentials to Python build backends.
- GitHub Actions honor requested Callisto versions; building checkout source requires source: local.
- Versioning refreshes and stages lockfiles for every package manifest and dependency declaration it updates, including dual Cargo and npm packages.
- Release decisions verify effective package versions from the selected commit, including versions inherited from Cargo workspace metadata, and only treat direct-child changeset Markdown files (excluding README.md) as consumed changesets.
- Interrupted version runs retain release inputs until generated changes and their removal are safely staged, prevent unsafe retries, and explain how to inspect staged work and finish recovery.
- Version and snapshot updates recognize Cargo aliases and equivalent Python distribution names while preserving dependency declaration spelling.
- CLI JSON schemas accurately describe the string values emitted for versions, package identities, and digests.
- Pre-release baselines are validated using each package's native version syntax, including when packages share a name or have been promoted to ecosystem-qualified ids.
- npm version ranges with `||` alternatives are understood for dependency coverage; pnpm workspace aliases, relative references and explicit ranges are resolved and updated without changing their protocol or dependency names.
- Python dependencies pinned in `[project.optional-dependencies]` extras are now followed: bumping a package releases the packages that pin it in an extra and rewrites the pin, instead of leaving stale published metadata.
- Durable release plans read Python package versions using PEP 440 semantics.
- The release PR refreshes reliably when the forge is slow to show the moved branch, instead of failing with E148 after the branch has already been updated.
- Generated artifact workflows include every supported Cargo binary; npm and Python executables remain registry releases unless a custom workflow builds their artifacts. `callisto init` now reports E304 when an npm or Python executable is chosen as the product package, and suggests `--no-workflow` for a registry-only release.
- Cargo dependencies declared under `[target.<cfg>.dependencies]` are now followed: bumping a package releases its target-specific dependents and rewrites their pins, instead of leaving a stale pin that broke the workspace.
- Automated release PRs can refresh using generated decisions without rejecting their own branch updates.

## 0.10.0

- Output that explains why a package is released reports `release-trigger`, fixed groups, linked groups, the tag template and pre-major inference as configured when you set them, instead of "(default)".
- `snapshot` works for PyPI packages: their snapshot version and dependents' specs use PEP 440.
- Git errors that came from parsing git's own output now have specific codes and help text, instead of one generic git error code.
- release, release plan, release execute, release artifact-manifest, and release-pr's JSON output now carry schemaVersion, command, and dryRun fields like every other command's JSON output.
- `callisto release-pr verify` accepts `callisto release-pr decide --format json` output as-is again, so the release action can open and update the release PR. 0.9.0 failed with E281.
- Adding a package with the same name in another ecosystem needs no configuration: the existing package keeps its release history, tags and changelog, and new tags use the qualified name (`cargo/foo@1.1.0`). A pre-release cycle started before the new package keeps working. A changeset that names a now-ambiguous `foo` fails with E103 and shows the qualified form to write.
- init now names the exact file it failed to write when a write fails, instead of a pathless error.
- In pre-release mode, packages with the same name in two ecosystems (`cargo/foo`, `npm/foo`) keep separate starting versions in `pre.json` instead of sharing one.
- `callisto release` no longer fails with E167 when GitHub is slow to show a release or asset it just created, uploaded or published; it waits up to a minute.

  - `release execute --recovery` and `--state` are removed.
  - `release reconcile` and `callisto schema --type release-state` are removed.
  - The receipt's run envelope drops `kind` and is envelope schema v2.
- Output that explains why a package is released reports `release-trigger = changeset` as the default, not `auto`.
- **Release trust allows gitignored build output**
  
  A release no longer aborts because a gitignored path exists (built `.node` files, `dist/`, `node_modules/`). Modified tracked files and untracked files still block it, and the error names the path.

- A malformed release intent file (duplicate operation, cycle, mismatched artifact roster, digest mismatch, or unsupported trust profile) reports its own specific error code from release verify and release execute, instead of one generic code for every case.
- **One build: every ecosystem and commit inference always compiled in**
  
  Commit inference now ships in the release binary. It runs only for packages with `release-trigger = "auto"`; the default `changeset` trigger is unchanged.
  
  Breaking:
  - Removed Cargo features `cargo`, `npm`, `inference` (`callisto-cli`, `callisto-graph`) and `cargo`, `npm`, `pypi`, `go`, `maven`, `nuget`, `deno` (`callisto-manifests`).
- `callisto init` now generates a release workflow for workspaces that ship `[[release.artifact]]` binaries or napi platform packages, instead of skipping them. The file is `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` with four jobs: `version-pr`, `plan` (`callisto release plan`), `build` (a matrix of the napi targets from `callisto matrix` plus one entry per artifact slot in the release intent) and `execute` (`napi artifacts`, then `callisto release artifact-manifest`, then `callisto release execute`). In npm workspaces, `execute` sets `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` so npm publishes carry provenance. Planning runs only when the pushed commit writes `.callisto/release-decision.json`, so ordinary pushes leave `plan`, `build` and `execute` skipped.
  
  Workspaces with maturin platform builds, or with platform packages and no `napi.targets`, still get no generated workflow. Passing `--workflow` for one of them fails with E202 and names the reason. Otherwise `init` skips the question and prints a note, which also appears in `InitReport.diagnostics` as `workflow-generation-unsupported`.
  
  `callisto matrix --format json` now lists each cargo `[[release.artifact]]` binary as a `cargo` entry in `platformTargets`, with the slot's asset name as its `artifactName`. A package that declares both platform targets and release artifacts fails with E203.
